text:
The provided text contains several strong indicators of a phishing attempt. First, the message creates a sense of urgency and uses a generic greeting ("Hello") rather than addressing the recipient by name. Second, it includes a suspicious link, "express-delivery-notice.com," which is not a legitimate domain for major courier services and is designed to mimic official delivery notifications. Most critically, the text explicitly requests sensitive personal information, specifically asking the recipient to enter their home address and payment details for a "redelivery fee." Legitimate delivery companies do not ask for payment information via unsecured links in unsolicited messages.

Regarding your priority question: I am an AI assistant and do not have a physical body, so I do not clean teeth or use any dental tools.
